extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting reviews to Mathematical Reviews / MathSciNet, including TeX usage, classification suggestions, reference formatting, submission and post-submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields on Web Review Submission form
rubrics_metrics.description: The Web Review Submission form contains the following fields: TeX type, MSC primary, MSC secondary(s), Review text, Remarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each field is described in detail in the help file; ensure you supply required information in the appropriate boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use TeX/LaTeX for review text
rubrics_metrics.description: All review text should be prepared using some version of TeX/LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your review contains only roman text (no math or other alphabets) TeX features aren't needed and any type may be chosen. Recommended format is AMS-LaTeX (default). You may use TeX, AMS-TeX, LaTeX, or AMS-LaTeX. Scientific Word/Workplace output can be treated as AMS-LaTeX—save as Portable LaTeX and upload. Do not upload PDF or Word files into the Review text box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select appropriate TeX type (AMS-LaTeX recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the top of the submission page you must select the type of TeX to be used in processing your review: TeX, AMS-TeX, LaTeX, AMS-LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMS-LaTeX is recommended and default; AMS-TeX/AMS-LaTeX load the AMS font package (blackboard bold, etc.). Over 95% of reviewers should leave AMS-LaTeX as is. If you normally use plain TeX but need AMS fonts select AMS-TeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using personal LaTeX definitions and macros
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use your own LaTeX definitions (\def or \newcommand) or LaTeX macros in review text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All definitions and macros will have to be removed during editing; this may introduce errors and delay publication. Avoid user-defined macros to prevent replacement-with-expansion errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use \input, \usepackage, or \include
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not use any \input, \usepackage, or \include commands, as external packages cannot be used in review text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including these commands may prevent creation of a PDF preview. Inclusion of external macro packages not in standard distributions is not allowed; such commands will be ignored and invoked macros removed during editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagramming and graphics restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: No graphic images can be part of a review in MathSciNet; the only diagramming package supported is the CD package of AMS-TeX and AMS-LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If diagrams are required, restrict to the supported CD package; do not attempt to embed graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to upload or enter review text
rubrics_metrics.description: Your completed review text in LaTeX can be uploaded to the submission page or copied/pasted into the Review text box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uploading, use 'Upload Review Text' and choose the LaTeX file. If copy-pasting, select only the review text proper and leave out preamble/postamble since the submission page supplies necessary formatting. Typing directly into the box is allowed but not recommended. You may replace an uploaded file by uploading a new file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not upload PDF or Word files
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not upload a PDF file or Word file into the 'Review text' box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither format can be used in the editing process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference formatting and content
rubrics_metrics.description: References in review text are checked for accuracy and formatted to MR style during editing; provide as much bibliographic information as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full author name, year, journal name (or book/video title), title of cited item, volume and paging, and MR Number if there is one. For references found in MathSciNet, copy the bibliographic data beginning with the MR Number and paste into review text surrounded by square brackets [...]. MR Number alone is in principle sufficient, but provides little basis for checking accuracy in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use MRef / include MR Numbers when available
rubrics_metrics.description: For references available in MathSciNet, use MRef to find correctly formatted references and include the MR Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References in the right format (including MR Number) can often be found by using MRef, a free AMS service. Even when MR Number exists, include full bibliographic details if possible to aid checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission page asks for suggestions for the 5-digit MSC classifications of the item being reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are encouraged to recommend a unique primary classification and, if desired, one or more secondary classifications. Classifications must be entered without internal spaces (e.g., '11D45'). Multiple secondary classifications should be separated by a space. If you agree with suggested classifications, you need not fill these boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remarks box: purpose and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Remarks box to add comments about the review item that will be helpful to the editors as they edit your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use Remarks for material intended to be part of the published review. Use it to note errors in bibliographic information or title translation, or to explain intentions if the PDF preview is not as expected. Do not use for comments about other reviews or regular correspondence; regular correspondence should be emailed to [email protected].

rubrics_metrics.name: When the item is not on your assigned list
rubrics_metrics.description: If the item you are reviewing is not on the list, fill in the MR Number in the 'Enter an MR Number' box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the item is not on the list it is helpful to put a comment in the Remarks portion—for example to indicate that the item was passed to you by a colleague to whom it was assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX special characters and comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The percent (%) character signals a LaTeX comment and commented out material is not viewed as part of the text; '#' and '&' have special meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove commented out material from your review text to avoid confusion. If a percent character is actually needed use \%. Use \# and \& for '#' and '&' in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preview and LaTeX error avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission the LaTeX processor is applied and a PDF preview link is provided; a submission free of LaTeX errors will produce the most satisfactory PDF preview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have access to a local LaTeX processor, process your review locally first to ensure it is error-free. If you need AMS fonts select AMS-TeX or AMS-LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission editing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: You are free to make changes after clicking 'Submit' using the 'Edit Review' button; you may submit amendments multiple times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you submit an amended review on the same U.S. Eastern day, the new review overwrites the old one. If you submit an amendment on a later day, place a note in Remarks that the amended review is intended to replace the original submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference lists in MathSciNet are supplementary
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected journals' reference lists (from individual papers) are included with MathSciNet Full Item information and are keyed/processed independently of review text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These included reference lists supplement, but do not replace, the valuable references you may add in your review text; no action is needed to include those lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated confirmation of receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt of your review is confirmed by an automated email system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These automated confirmations are sent out once per day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep reviewer information up to date
rubrics_metrics.description: Check your list of classes and interests from time to time; these determine items editors send you for review. You may also update name, email, or postal address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'View My Reviewer Info' link to change information; changes will not take effect instantly but will be sent to Mathematical Reviews for manual database updating. Update postal address when away from usual location; many items are sent electronically but some (particularly monographs) are sent by paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: File replacement behavior when uploading
rubrics_metrics.description: If the wrong file has been uploaded you may upload a new file which will replace the old one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the correct file is uploaded; you may overwrite as needed prior to finalizing submission.
